issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect an instance method named addRating(stars:) (external parameter label 'stars'). The template declares func addRating(stars: Int) accordingly. However, the solution's Course implementation defines func addRating(rating: Int) while the solution's Client calls addRating(stars: ...). This mismatch between the method's parameter label in Course and its usage in Client (and the problem spec) is a structural inconsistency that will cause compilation errors and confuse students about the correct signature to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Course method signature consistent with the problem statement and client usage. Change the solution's Course method to use the 'stars' parameter label (e.g. func addRating(stars: Int) { ... }) or update all call sites and the problem statement to use the same label. Ensure template, solution Course implementation, and Client call sites all use the identical external parameter name.

issues.description: The method parameter label for the course rating is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement and the template declare/use addRating(stars:), but the solution's Course implementation defines addRating(rating:), while the solution's Client still calls addRating(stars:). This mismatch between the parameter label 'stars' and 'rating' breaks the 1:1 mapping students expect and can cause confusion (and compilation mismatch) when comparing the problem, template, and solution code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the parameter label consistent across all artifacts. Prefer matching the problem statement and template: change the solution Course method signature to func addRating(stars: Int) { ... } (and update any internal references) so that Client calls and the implementation use the same label.
